Thank you very much for the update! I gave it a try and this is what a found:

- Resizing the window works great now!
- When embedded, I have to double click inside the game window for it to start registering input, which is a bit cumbersome. This isn't the case when the game is not embedded.
![CleanShot 2025-05-02 at 15 25 45](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd1c2e60-4bad-49c8-98b3-38fa3689ecff)

- On Windows, when you change the window mode to something other than windowed at runtime, you get a message saying `Embedded window only supports Windowed mode.` This message doesn't seem to appear here.
- The game may keep registering inputs after clicking outside of it. In the video below you can see all my inputs. I start pressing D, moving to the left. Then I click the remote scene tree and afterwards I stop pressing D. The game thinks I keep pressing D, though I don't. It only stops registering this Input when I click back into the game and press and release D one more time. If I had to guess, this may be because the game process doesn't get the information that the D button has been released when its not focused.  On Windows, the button gets released when clicking outside the game window. I've attached this project so it's more convenient for you to replicate this issue. 

![CleanShot 2025-05-02 at 10 18 19](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6dd9d381-a37a-407f-8086-e031611870e8)

@stuartcarnie 

Thank you for the fixes, feels great!

Another thing I've noticed is that when you click outside of the embedded game, you have to click inside the embedded game again for it to start registering inputs. You can't just hover over it like on Windows. But this is a general limitation of macOS, right?

> I can't reproduce this, even with your MRP and pressing the 1, 2 or 3 keys. Can you provide more info for this?

I think my other project was just broken. It was too big to zip and upload, so I deleted some files to upload it but now it works as expected. I tested some of my other projects and there were no issues.

> I can add a log for that, but it is just ignored if you try

I think its fine as is! The log on Windows looks a bit out of place to me because it's just a default console output instead of a warning. Except for the initial build and rendering information, I can't think of another situation where Godot prints to the console.

> Another thing I've noticed is that when you click outside of the embedded game, you have to click inside the embedded game again for it to start registering inputs. You can't just hover over it like on Windows. But this is a general limitation of macOS, right?

No, I removed a behaviour that was similar, but it was confusing and not explicit. For example, a user might be moving the mouse across the Godot Editor window to the other side to click on something in the editor, but don't want the mouse events to be sent to the game window, which might alter its state. With the hover mode, it would start sending mouse events to the game window, unintentionally. This approach allows the user to decide when they want to refocus, which is mostly the same as if the game was running in a separate window.
